subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Design is architecturally sound and consistent with the codebase's established evidence-enforcement model (structure at prep via rq-PR010, resolution at completion/acceptance via checkCompletedTaskEvidencePlan + checkUnresolvedVerificationEvidence). KD2's gate-binding for respects evidence matches the existing implements/verifies pattern, so 'block everywhere / no grandfathering' is satisfied architecturally (every task's respects evidence is evaluated at the next acceptance/release gate; AC3 'completion/gate' both resolve there in the current model). The KD4 reducer substrate is correctly identified and command-level replay-safe because no workflow handler branches on retry state to emit commands (workflows.ts:615-678 are read-projections; readyForAcceptance uses incompleteTaskCount). Authority machinery (task-classifier.ts:387-394) genuinely requires adv-reviewer, so self-assertion is blocked. Spec-law: no spec contradicted; KD4 must keep rq-loopLedger01 retryFailureCount consistent (it derives from the same error_recovery substrate). Three substance-level concerns: (1) KD1 underspecified for test-route tasks claiming respects on review-policy avoidances (review_evidence_ref machinery is non-test-gated); (2) KD4 retry_count semantics change does not address rq-loopLedger01 consistency; (3) the design's own P38 lever-citations carry wrong directory prefixes (substance/line-numbers correct, paths wrong), undermining DDC5/AC5 anchor exactness. required_validation_consistency.status = caution = validation.status (both caution).

validation.notes: No fail-level blockers: every objective satisfiable, no constraint violated at design level; all lever-citation SUBSTANCE verified (line numbers correct). Cautions (implementation must address): [C-AUTH] KD1/KD2 respects-evidence enforcement underspecified for test-evidence_policy tasks claiming respects — task-classifier.ts:372-377 gates review_evidence_ref on non-test policy; a test-route task claiming respects on a review-policy avoidance has no review_evidence_ref, so authority path undefined (AC3, objective 2). [C-LOOPLEDGER] KD4 retry_count semantics change must keep rq-loopLedger01 retryFailureCount consistent and not change retry budgets (AC6, C7). [C-REPLAY] KD4 reducer-logic change must keep replay-determinism.test.ts green at command-sequence level; progress_rounds Zod field must be optional/default [] for in-flight workflow migration (C7, DDC2). [C-PATHS] Design cites wrong dirs for 5 files (temporal/contract-mint->validator/, temporal/subagent-report->tools/, temporal/tool-formatters->utils/, types/store-types->storage/, bare task.ts->tools/) — fix before implementation since DDC5/AC5 anchors require exact paths and C5 mandates P38 trace (C5, AC5, DDC5). requirement.title: Respects claims on avoidance/out_of_scope items require non-claiming review authority
requirement.body: A task's contract_refs.respects claim targeting an avoidance (DONT) or out_of_scope (OOS) contract item is a positive compliance assertion that the claiming agent cannot self-certify. At acceptance and release gate readiness, every done task with such a respects claim MUST carry task-scoped review authority from a non-claiming agent (adv-reviewer). A change-scoped review report does not qualify — the reviewer must have examined THIS task. Self-asserted compliance alone MUST fail with a typed RESPECTS_EVIDENCE_AUTHORITY_MISSING blocker. The check applies to ALL done tasks (no grandfathering); existing recorded review evidence is accepted, not re-litigated. A task whose evidence_policy is 'test' is not exempt: respects on avoidance/OOS items requires review authority regardless of the task's own evidence route.

requirement.title: adv_change_create surfaces bounded portfolio state with graceful degradation
requirement.body: adv_change_create MUST surface bounded portfolio state at creation time: non-terminal change count, never-terminal share, and a soft nudge above threshold. Change creation is where reflexive change creation happens; surfacing the portfolio at that moment gives the creating agent the state it needs to consider the durable middle tier (adv_backlog_add). The portfolio read is deadline-capped (well under the store budget) and MUST degrade to an explicit { available: false } marker on any failure or timeout — creation is never blocked by the portfolio read. The nudge fires only above BOTH thresholds (minimum open count AND never-terminal share) so small portfolios stay quiet. An empty portfolio reports zero share with no nudge.

documents.proposal:
# Fix finding routing

## Why

ADV has a correct two-tier sink for findings — adv_backlog_add (candidate) vs adv_change_create (commitment), bridged by adv_backlog_promote — but the workflow only routes findings to the candidate tier during proposal and discovery. From design onward, the only durable sink any command names is change-creation, so ADV generates change accumulation it cannot clear. Measured in decideWorkflowHibernation: 10.71 new changes/day x 38% never-terminal = 4.07 permanently-running entities/day; that change then created 3 more changes in its own prep phase.

Unifying theme: ADV constraints and counters record CLAIMS rather than establishing FACTS. Three symptom families, one root shape:

- DONT/OOS contract items are declarative and never evaluated: an agent attached respects [DONT3, C1, OOS4, OOS3] to the very task DONT3 was written to prevent, and the system stored the claim of compliance without checking it (D3).
- The doom-loop retry guard reads a surface signal (a BLOCKED verdict) as if it established a fact (the fix failed): on tk-f7fcf367f261, five adv-reviewer rounds each found a DISTINCT genuine defect (findings converged 4->1->3->1->1->0), yet each BLOCKED verdict incremented retry_count until the guard hard-blocked further report submission — the better the reviewer performed, the faster it bricked its own ability to report (D6).

All drivers verified against source (2026-08-05, P38 trace):

- D1: adv_backlog_add IS callable mid-lifecycle — `visibility.lifecycle` is consumed only by manifest generation, catalog display, and tests; no dispatch-time phase gate exists (tool-registry.ts:1172). The binding constraint is that no command from design onward mentions the backlog.
- D2: prep MoSCoW Won't path is prose-only (.opencode/command/adv-prep.md:340).
- D3: respects refs get referential-integrity validation only (plugin/src/tools/task.ts:192-206); the five ContractConflictKind values (plugin/src/types/tasks.ts:119-125) are declared in a Zod enum and never produced by any production code; no tool-call/mutation audit log exists on Task or subagent reports; adv_contract_mint warrants check declared capability existence at mint time, not behavior.
- D4: adv_change_create computes no portfolio state; hydration stats live on show/list paths only.
- D5: design risk-table idiom made change-creation the self-evident mitigation for "finding is lost" (.opencode/command/adv-design.md:127).
- D6: the hard-brick mechanism (write a record the read path rejects) was CLOSED by clampDoomLoopAccumulator (reducer clamp at change-state.ts:2042+, report-side clamp at subagent-report.ts:419-424, shared budget constant). RESIDUAL defect is accounting semantics: retry_count still increments per BLOCKED verdict regardless of finding novelty; the guard cannot distinguish repeated attempts at one broken fix from successive discovery of new real defects; the doom-loop UX (tool-formatters.ts:699-724) still reads the conflated count as failure.

## What Changes

- Backlog routing appears in command vocabulary from design onward (D1): design, prep, apply, review, harden commands name adv_backlog_add as the durable low-commitment sink for out-of-scope findings.
- Prep MoSCoW Won't path gains the backlog as the middle option between prose and a change (D2).
- Design risk-table framing restated: the risk is the finding being lost; the mitigation is a durable record, not a committed work item (D5).
- DONT/OOS contract items become evaluative rather than self-asserted (D3) — mechanism chosen at design; must be machine-checked, not prose. Enforcement blocks on ALL tasks carrying respects claims (user decision: no grandfathering); design must provide a transition/remediation path for in-flight tasks (attach reviewer evidence) and must never brick persistence of the report explaining a violation.
- adv_change_create surfaces portfolio state as stats plus a soft warning above a threshold (D4; user decision); no hard block without evidence a soft signal failed.
- Retry accounting distinguishes progress from failure (D6): a BLOCKED verdict whose blocking findings share no id/fingerprint with the previous round's findings is treated as progress, not a retry; report submission degrades to a warning rather than a hard block at/over budget (belt-and-suspenders behind the shipped clamp). NOT fixed by raising max_retries.

## User Outcomes

- An agent (or user) working inside a change who surfaces an out-of-scope finding has an obvious, named, durable place to put it that is not a new change — at every phase, not just early ones.
- Users see fewer reflexively-created changes accumulating; the backlog becomes the visible middle tier it was designed to be.
- Contract avoidances and out-of-scope items stop passing silently on self-asserted claims; violations surface.
- A productive review round — one that finds new real defects — is never again counted as a failed retry, and the report explaining a guard firing is always preservable.
- Change-creation stays easy; the system is honest about portfolio state at the moment of creation without blocking legitimate work.

## Affected Code

- `.opencode/command/adv-prep.md` — MoSCoW Won't path gains backlog routing (D2)
- `.opencode/command/adv-design.md` — risk-table framing + backlog routing (D5, D1)
- `.opencode/command/adv-apply.md`, `adv-review.md`, `adv-harden.md` — backlog routing vocabulary (D1; exact placement at design)
- `plugin/src/tools/task.ts`, `plugin/src/validator/contract.ts`, `plugin/src/types/tasks.ts` — D3 evaluative mechanism (respects/conflict machinery; ContractConflictKind vocabulary is dormant and available to build on)
- `plugin/src/tools/change.ts` (adv_change_create) — D4 portfolio-state line
- `plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts` (applySubagentReportSubmittedToState reducer), `plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts` (report submission), `plugin/src/utils/tool-formatters.ts` (doom-loop UX), `plugin/src/types/tasks.ts` (error_recovery schema) — D6 progress-vs-retry accounting
- Possibly `plugin/src/tools/backlog-shell.ts` / `plugin/src/types/future-work.ts` — context packet surface, only if the chosen D1/D3 design needs it

## Related Repositories

None — plugin repo only.

## Constraints

- Any D3 fix must be evaluative, not declarative. A new prose rule is not a fix; D3 is the evidence prose rules do not bind.
- Do not make change-creation harder in a way that pushes agents back to losing findings in prose. The goal is a correctly-priced middle tier, not friction.
- Do not treat the 3 changes created in decideWorkflowHibernation as the defect. They were judged warranted; the defect is the reflex, not the outcome.
- D6: a retry guard must never hard-block persistence of the report that explains why it fired — degrade to a warning. Do not fix the guard by raising max_retries (hides the signal instead of teaching the counter to read it).
- P38: trace every mechanism from declaration through its consumer to an observable effect before asserting what it does.
- Zod schemas authoritative: run `pnpm run schemas:generate` after public schema changes, keep `pnpm run schemas:check` green; run `pnpm run generate:manifests` after editing tool-role-policy.ts.
- Tests via root `bin/oc-test`, not vitest directly.

## Impact

- Command docs (up to 5 files), contract/task validation machinery, change-create result shape, retry-accounting reducer + report submission path.
- D3 enforcement applies to all tasks carrying respects claims (no grandfathering — user decision): in-flight tasks with self-asserted refs become non-compliant at next evaluation until reviewer evidence (or machine check) is attached. Design must make the remediation path obvious and cheap, and must not retroactively invalidate COMPLETED tasks' recorded evidence.
- D6 reducer change alters how state is derived from history — replay-determinism suite must prove already-recorded histories still re-derive valid state (same discipline clampDoomLoopAccumulator applied).

## Risks

- D3 mechanism could drift into prose-shaped enforcement (a "better warning") — mitigated by the evaluative hard constraint and by preferring structural checks over text interpretation.
- No-grandfathering D3 enforcement could stall in-flight work that claimed respects under the declarative regime — mitigated by a designed remediation path (attach reviewer evidence at next gate), surfaced loudly at release notes.
- D6 progress-detection could misclassify a genuine repeated failure as progress if finding fingerprints are unstable — mitigated by conservative fingerprinting (design decision: prefer id match, fall back to normalized text fingerprint; when uncertain, count as retry).
- Portfolio-state line at create time adds read cost on a contended store — keep it cheap/bounded and degrade gracefully (observed live: change_list archive reads exceed their 8s deadline under multi-session load).

1. In-flight tasks with self-asserted refs (no grandfathering — user decision): they become non-compliant at next evaluation. Transition must make remediation (attach reviewer evidence) obvious; completed tasks' recorded evidence is not retroactively invalidated.
2. Ordering — reviewer evidence for a respects claim may arrive after checkpoint; binding evaluation to the wrong moment either blocks legitimate completion or never fires.
3. False positive — a legitimate task textually resembling a DONT item (e.g. editing the backlog tool while a DONT says "do not extend the backlog surface").

D4 (portfolio line):
1. Read timeout — the portfolio read fails/stalls under contention (observed live); the line must degrade to an honest "unavailable" without blocking creation.
2. Threshold semantics — 50+ mostly-stale drafts make raw counts noisy; a naive threshold trains agents to ignore the warning.

D6 (retry accounting):
1. Fingerprint instability — a reviewer re-words the same finding across rounds; unstable fingerprints misclassify a repeated failure as progress. Conservative rule needed: exact-id match, then normalized-text fingerprint, else count as retry.
2. Genuine doom loop with rotating phrasing — an agent rationalizing past a guard produces "new" findings each round; progress classification must not become the escape hatch the guard exists to close (cap progress exemptions; surface classification to user at doom-loop threshold either way).
3. Reducer change vs replay — histories recorded pre-change must still re-derive valid state (replay-determinism suite).

### Open Design Questions

1. **D3 mechanism choice** — trust: joint (strictness resolved by user: block everywhere, no grandfathering); blast radius: false blocks on task completion across all changes; alternatives: (a) gate-time shape evaluator, (b) reviewer-owned evidence for respects claims [machinery shipped in fixReviewerEvidence], (c) narrow machine-check for tool-forbidding DONT items [no audit log exists today], (b)+lite(c). Recommendation: (b) primary — enforce the evidencePolicy already declared at mint — with (c) deferred to its own change once a tool-call substrate exists.
2. **Where D3 evaluation binds** — trust: agent; blast radius: binding at checkpoint blocks completion paths (3 write surfaces), binding at gate-readiness is broader; alternatives: write-time, checkpoint-time, gate-time. Resolve at design.
3. **D3 transition path for in-flight tasks** — trust: agent (user decided strictness); blast radius: stalled in-flight work; alternatives: require evidence at next gate eval with loud remediation text; bulk-mark legacy refs advisory-by-age. Recommendation: former + release-note surfacing.
4. **D4 line content + threshold** — trust: agent (user decided stats + soft warning); blast radius: noisy line trains ignoring; alternatives: raw counts vs staleness-weighted vs threshold-only warning. Resolve at design with cheap-stats check.
5. **D6 finding fingerprint** — trust: agent; blast radius: misclassification either direction; alternatives: id-only, id + normalized text, reviewer-supplied novelty flag. Recommendation: id-first with normalized-text fallback, uncertain => retry (conservative).
6. **D6 progress-exemption cap** — trust: agent; blast radius: guard bypass; alternatives: unbounded progress rounds, capped consecutive progress rounds before mandatory user surface. Recommendation: classification always surfaced at doom-loop threshold regardless of progress/retry split.

### Draft Spec Deltas

- `rq-findingRouting01` — Given an agent operating in design, prep, apply, review, or harden phase, when the command contract addresses out-of-scope findings, then the contract names adv_backlog_add as the durable middle-tier sink and adv_backlog_promote as the commitment bridge. (Anchors: per-command asset tests.)
- `rq-respectsEvaluation01` — Given a task carrying contract_refs.respects to avoidance or out_of_scope items, when the task approaches completion or gate evaluation, then compliance with those items is established by an authority other than the claiming agent (reviewer-owned evidence per the declared evidencePolicy, or a machine check), not by the stored claim. Applies to all tasks; transition path for pre-existing refs is part of the design.
- `rq-createPortfolioLine01` — Given an adv_change_create invocation, when the result is returned, then it includes a bounded portfolio-state line (non-terminal count, never-terminal share if cheaply materialized) with a soft warning above a threshold; the line degrades to an explicit unavailable marker on read failure and never blocks creation.
- `rq-retryProgressAccounting01` — Given successive BLOCKED reviewer verdicts on one task, when a new verdict's blocking findings share no id or stable fingerprint with the previous round's, then the guard records progress rather than incrementing the retry count; and when the count reaches budget, report submission degrades to a warning rather than a hard block. Raising max_retries is not a fix.

### Related Pattern Scan (P25)

Class 1 — self-asserted claims stored without evaluation: matches = contract item `warrants` (resolved at mint, never consumed post-mint), `ContractConflictKind` enum (declared, no producer), `evidencePolicy` on contract items (declared, unenforced), `not_applicable_reason` (stored, never cross-checked), retry_count (incremented on surface signal). Same class repeats across the contract + guard surfaces; this change addresses the respects and retry instances.
Class 2 — finding-sink vocabulary: matches = zero command files outside proposal/triage name the backlog (verified by grep).

### Completeness Verification

- Problem-completeness: the observed symptoms (3 reflexive changes; bricked report submission) are instances of the verified claims-vs-facts class across routing, contract, and guard surfaces. D6 arrived mid-flight, was verified against current source (brick closed by clamp; residual = semantics), and was pulled into scope by user decision. Confidence: high.
- Solution-scope: in-scope solution spans docs + contract/task machinery + create result + retry reducer/submission. NO sole-chokepoint claim is made; the trace enumerated 3 contract_refs write surfaces and multiple guard read/write sites — any D3/D6 design claiming a single chokepoint must verify it with a surface scan at design time (sole-entry rule applies there, not blocking here).
- Secondary-surface dispositions: adv_task_update recovery path (mutateRecoveredTask) — IN SCOPE for D3 evaluation design. gate-readiness coverage projection — IN SCOPE as evaluation-surface option. adv_contract_mint parser changes — OUT OF SCOPE except additive variant support if design requires. adv_backlog_add dedupe — OUT OF SCOPE (accept-and-triage). doom-loop UX text beyond classification surfacing — OUT OF SCOPE.

### LBP Check

Internal mechanism change; no external alternative is viable (explicit skip of external-solution check). Direction matches long-term best practice: P33 structural-over-heuristic, existing authority-boundary machinery (fixReviewerEvidence), instructions-audit test-or-cut for new command claims, P38 trace discipline applied to every load-bearing claim, clamp's replay-determinism discipline reused for D6.

### AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS

Coverage: B:C F:C S:C M:C

- M1 LOW Missing Information: cheap-portfolio-stats question for D4 unresolved (design input, Open Design Questions Q4). Evidence: "Portfolio-state line at create time adds read cost on a contended store — keep it cheap/bounded and degrade gracefully". Reason: non-blocking; design resolves.

No CRITICAL, no HIGH → proceed to agreement.

## Discovery Agenda

- D3 mechanism selection: options (a)/(b)/(c) evaluated against trace findings — resolved to recommendation (b) primary (reviewer-owned evidence enforcing the mint-declared evidencePolicy), (c) deferred until a tool-call substrate exists. Final mechanism at design.
- Exact placement of backlog routing in each command file (design/prep/apply/review/harden) — design.
- What portfolio stats are cheaply available at adv_change_create time — design (hydration stats materialized on show/list; visibility claim queries exist for triage).
- Compat: does tightening respects validation affect in-flight changes with existing self-asserted refs — RESOLVED by user: enforcement applies everywhere; transition path is a design deliverable.
- Whether D6 lands in clampDoomLoopAccumulator or needs its own change — RESOLVED: clamp archived without absorbing semantics; D6 pulled into THIS change by user at Phase 4.5.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Command-vocabulary backlog routing from design onward (D1, D2, D5 — doc edits, each with drift-guard anchors per instructions-audit test-or-cut)
- Evaluative D3 mechanism for DONT/OOS respects claims — enforced on all tasks (no grandfathering), with a designed transition/remediation path for in-flight refs
- Portfolio-state surfacing (stats + soft warning above threshold) in adv_change_create result (D4)
- D6 retry-accounting semantics: progress-vs-retry discrimination by finding identity, degrade-to-warning at budget, no max_retries raise

### Out of Scope

- Hard admission control / blocking change creation on portfolio state
- Retroactive invalidation of COMPLETED tasks' recorded evidence
- A general tool-call audit platform (only the substrate the chosen D3 mechanism requires; option (c) deferred to its own change)
- adv_backlog_add dedupe machinery
- adv_contract_mint parser rebuild (additive variant support only if design requires)
- Doom-loop UX redesign beyond classification surfacing
- Whether 3 is the right retry budget (unchanged from clamp's scope)

### Must Not

- Must not add another prose avoidance/rule as the D3 fix
- Must not make change-creation harder in a way that pushes findings back into prose
- Must not create changes reflexively while implementing this — findings surfaced during this change go to the backlog, per the discipline being built
- Must not fix D6 by raising max_retries
- Must not let any guard (D3 evaluation or D6 budget) hard-block persistence of the report that explains why it fired

## Root Cause Analysis

**Defect origin:** ADV generates change accumulation it cannot clear, and its constraints/counters record claims rather than establishing facts. Findings surfaced mid-lifecycle have no named durable sink other than change-creation; contract avoidance/out-of-scope items are stored as self-asserted claims that are never evaluated; the retry guard reads a BLOCKED verdict as proof a fix failed.

**Evidence gathered:**

- Tier 1 (local): decideWorkflowHibernation measured 10.71 new changes/day x 38% never-terminal = 4.07 permanently-running entities/day, then created 3 changes in its own prep phase. tk-f7fcf367f261: five reviewer rounds each finding distinct genuine defects (4->1->3->1->1->0) counted as retries until report submission hard-blocked. Verified this session: adv_backlog_add lifecycle label descriptive-only (tool-registry.ts:1172); respects referential-integrity only (task.ts:192-206); ContractConflictKind enum no production producer (types/tasks.ts:119-125); no tool-call audit field exists (broad search, zero production matches); adv_change_create computes no portfolio state; adv-prep.md:340 Won't path prose; adv-design.md:127 risk-table idiom; avoidance items declare evidencePolicy:"review" + verificationRequired:true at mint (contract-mint.ts:41-90) with no enforcing consumer; retry brick closed by clamp (change-state.ts:2042+, subagent-report.ts:419-424) but accounting semantics unchanged.
- Tier 2 (external): not applicable — internal mechanism defect.

**Leading hypothesis:** One root shape with two reinforcing instances. (1) Command vocabulary only names the backlog during proposal/discovery, so the cheap sink is invisible exactly when most findings surface. (2) Negative contract space and guard counters are declarative — the system stores the CLAIM (respects ref; BLOCKED verdict) and never checks it against the FACT (task behavior; finding novelty), so guardrails do not bind and productive work reads as failure.

**Ruled-out paths:** Tool lifecycle enforcement (verified absent — not the constraint). The 3 hibernation changes themselves (judged warranted; the reflex is the defect). Stronger prose warnings (D3 is the evidence prose does not bind). Raising max_retries (hides the signal). Hard-blocking change creation (deferred without evidence a soft signal failed). Treating the D6 brick as the residual defect (clamp closed it; semantics remain).

**Spec-law impact:** Change-required for the D3 evaluative mechanism and D6 accounting (advance-workflow spec governs contract/gate/guard behavior); the D1/D2/D5 doc routing may be docs-only with asset-test anchors. Confirm at design per /adv-problem Phase 5.

**Bypass rationale (RCA inline rather than /adv-problem):** the promoted backlog item carried a full root-cause analysis in its context packet, and every load-bearing claim was independently re-verified against source in this session before framing — the RCA evidence bar is met without a second loop.

# Agreement

## Objectives

1. Mid-lifecycle agents have a named, durable, low-commitment sink for out-of-scope findings at every phase from design onward (D1/D2/D5).
2. DONT/OOS contract items are evaluated by an authority other than the claiming agent; self-asserted compliance no longer passes silently (D3).
3. Change creation surfaces portfolio state honestly without friction (D4).
4. The retry guard distinguishes productive review rounds from failed fixes and never hard-blocks preservation of the report that explains why it fired (D6).
5. New routing claims in command docs carry drift-guard anchors (instructions-audit test-or-cut).

## Success Criteria

1. SC1: An agent reading any of the design/prep/apply/review/harden command contracts can identify adv_backlog_add as the durable sink for an out-of-scope finding without prior knowledge.
2. SC2: A task claiming respects on a DONT/OOS item cannot complete on the claim alone — an authority other than the claiming agent establishes compliance, on every task including pre-existing ones, with a documented remediation path.
3. SC3: adv_change_create results include portfolio state (stats + soft warning above threshold); a store read failure produces an explicit degraded marker, never a creation failure.
4. SC4: D1/D2/D5 routing text survives refactors — drift-guard tests fail if the routing claims are removed or contradicted.
5. SC5: A reviewer who finds a NEW genuine defect each round can always submit the report; successive novel-defect rounds record as progress, not retries; at budget, submission degrades to a warning, never a hard block.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AC1: Given an out-of-scope finding surfaced during prep, when the agent follows the MoSCoW Won't path, then the contract directs it to adv_backlog_add as the durable middle-tier option (asset test).
2. AC2: Given a design risk-table entry for a finding that might be lost, when the mitigation is framed, then the adv-design contract requires durable-record framing, not no-change-owns-it (asset test).
3. AC3: Given a task with contract_refs.respects referencing avoidance/out_of_scope items and no evidence from a non-claiming authority, when the task approaches completion or gate evaluation, then the self-asserted claim alone fails (validator test).
4. AC4: Given adv_change_create under a failing/slow portfolio read, when the read exceeds its budget, then creation succeeds and the result carries an explicit unavailable marker (test). [warrant: tool:adv_change_create]
5. AC5: Given the new routing claims in the five command files, when asset tests run, then each claim has a fidelity anchor that fails on removal (test).
6. AC6: Given two successive BLOCKED verdicts whose blocking findings share no id or stable fingerprint, when the second is recorded, then the guard records progress rather than incrementing the retry count (reducer test).
7. AC7: Given a task at/over retry budget, when a sub-agent report is submitted, then submission succeeds with a warning marker rather than a hard write block (test). [warrant: tool:adv_subagent_report_submit]

## Constraints

- C1: Any D3 fix must be evaluative, not declarative. A new prose rule is not a fix; D3 is the evidence prose rules do not bind.
- C2: Do not make change-creation harder in a way that pushes agents back to losing findings in prose. The goal is a correctly-priced middle tier, not friction.
- C3: Do not treat the 3 changes created in decideWorkflowHibernation as the defect. They were judged warranted; the defect is the reflex, not the outcome.
- C4: A retry guard must never hard-block persistence of the report that explains why it fired — degrade to a warning. Do not fix the guard by raising max_retries (hides the signal instead of teaching the counter to read it).
- C5: P38 — trace every mechanism from declaration through its consumer to an observable effect before asserting what it does.
- C6: Zod schemas authoritative: run `pnpm run schemas:generate` after public schema changes, keep `pnpm run schemas:check` green; run `pnpm run generate:manifests` after editing tool-role-policy.ts.
- C7: Tests via root `bin/oc-test`, not vitest directly. D6 reducer change must pass the replay-determinism suite (histories recorded pre-change still re-derive valid state).

## Avoidances

- DONT1: Do not add another prose avoidance/rule as the D3 fix.
- DONT2: Do not make change-creation harder in a way that pushes findings back into prose.
- DONT3: Do not create changes reflexively while implementing this — findings surfaced during this change go to the backlog, per the discipline being built.
- DONT4: Do not fix D6 by raising max_retries.
- DONT5: Do not let any guard (D3 evaluation or D6 budget) hard-block persistence of the report that explains why it fired.
- OOS1: Hard admission control / blocking change creation on portfolio state is out of scope.
- OOS2: Retroactive invalidation of COMPLETED tasks' recorded evidence is out of scope (only pre-completion enforcement; completed tasks are not re-litigated).
- OOS3: A general tool-call audit platform is out of scope (only the substrate the chosen D3 mechanism requires; option (c) deferred to its own change).
- OOS4: adv_backlog_add dedupe machinery is out of scope (accept-and-triage).
- OOS5: adv_contract_mint parser rebuild is out of scope (additive variant support only if design requires).
- OOS6: Doom-loop UX redesign beyond classification surfacing is out of scope.
- OOS7: Whether 3 is the right retry budget is out of scope (unchanged from clamp's scope).

## Preview Applicability

Option (c) requires a tool-call audit log that does not exist and is deferred to its own change.
2. **Backlog dedupe = accept-and-triage.** Rationale: dedupe machinery is its own problem; pulling it in would grow scope against the friction/size intent.
3. **D6 finding fingerprint = id-first, normalized-text fallback, uncertain ⇒ count as retry.** Rationale: conservative on the side the guard exists to close; surfaces to user at doom-loop threshold regardless.

5. **Routing placement in command files = deferred to design.** Rationale: exact placement is a per-command design decision (Phase boundaries, sink-citation form, anchor-test shape); discovery established the WHAT, design owns the WHERE/HOW.

## Deferred Questions

None — all open questions resolved at Phase 4.5; routing placement and D4 line content/threshold specifics are design inputs (recorded in Discovery Agenda / Open Design Questions), not deferred user decisions.

## Sign-Off

Criteria approved at discovery Phase 4.5.1 (Tier A `approve`, 2026-08-05). Agreement persisted at Phase 4.6.

# Design

## Architecture Overview

Three coordinated edits, one root shape (claims recorded rather than established):

1. **Vocabulary (D1/D2/D5)** — command-contract prose names `adv_backlog_add` as the durable middle-tier sink from design onward; each new load-bearing claim gets a drift-guard asset test (instructions-audit test-or-cut). No runtime change; the lever is the agent reading the contract.
2. **Evaluation (D3)** — enforce the `evidencePolicy` already declared on avoidance items at mint. Extend the existing evidence-requirement check to cover `contract_refs.respects` claims on avoidance items, reusing the fixReviewerEvidence authority machinery. Option (c) machine-check is deferred (no tool-call log exists).
3. **Honesty (D4/D6)** — `adv_change_create` surfaces bounded portfolio state; the retry reducer discriminates progress from failure by finding identity and the clamp emits an explicit warning marker.

No new persistence substrate. D3 and D6 build on existing fields and existing enforcement surfaces.

## Lever Citations (P38 — call sites, not declarations; paths corrected per validator C-PATHS)

|---|---|---|
| D3 evidence requirement for implements/verifies (the path to extend) | `plugin/src/temporal/gate-readiness.ts:706-788` `checkUnresolvedVerificationEvidence(state, gateId)` (+ sibling `checkCompletedTaskEvidencePlan` :800, also acceptance/release-only) — iterates done tasks, skips non-proof-bearing policies, reads `review_evidence_ref` + `consumer_warnings` + typed `verification[]`; emits the unresolved-evidence blocker at acceptance/release | verified |
| D3 stage-v2 completion validator (authority gate) | `plugin/src/validator/task-classifier.ts:372-395` `validateTaskEvidenceForStage` — requires `agent === "adv-reviewer"` + task_id match; claiming agents (orchestrator/adv-engineer) cannot self-assert | verified |
| D3 authority boundary to reuse | `plugin/src/types/evidence-policy.ts:35-81` — `PROOF_BEARING_EVIDENCE_POLICIES = [test, static_check, review, artifact_reference]` (review IS proof-bearing) + authority resolution | verified |
| D3 declared-but-unenforced policy on avoidance items | `plugin/src/validator/contract-mint.ts:41-90` mints avoidance items with `evidencePolicy:"review"`, `verificationRequired:true`; **no consumer reads these post-mint** (negative finding — the gap) | verified |
| D3 task write surfaces (3, same referential validator) | `plugin/src/tools/task.ts:1554` (add), `:1207-1209` (update signal), `:1024-1026` (recovery) | verified |
| D6 retry reducer | `plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts` `applySubagentReportSubmittedToState` (~2042-2089) — increments retry_count/attempts on verdict+attempt number, does NOT inspect finding content; `totalAttempts` monotonic | verified |
| D6 report-side clamp | `plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts:419-424` — `retry_count: Math.min(attempt, SUBAGENT_REPORT_MAX_RETRIES)`; currently silent (no warning marker — confirmed by validator) | verified |
| D6 doom-loop UX | `plugin/src/utils/tool-formatters.ts:699-724` — reads `retry_count >= max_retries` only (not narrower_retry_count, not findings) | verified |
| D6 narrower_retry_count (NOT the progress substrate) | `plugin/src/types/tasks.ts:394-418`, `plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts:246-325` — bounded (≤1) delegation-recovery counter, not a progress counter | verified |
| D6 loop-ledger projection (consistency requirement) | `rq-loopLedger01` derives `retryFailureCount` from `error_recovery` — KD4's retry_count semantics must keep this projection consistent | verified (spec) |
| D4 create-result shape | `plugin/src/tools/change.ts:2766+` (adv_change_create result assembly); `ChangeCreateResult` (`plugin/src/storage/store-types.ts:191-200`) has no portfolioState field | verified |
| D1/D2/D5 anchor pattern | per-command `*-assets.test.ts` files assert command-file content (exact example file:line to confirm at prep; pattern verified present via adv-triage-portfolio-assets.test.ts) | pattern verified |

## Key Decisions

### KD1 — D3 mechanism = enforce the declared evidencePolicy (option b), not a new evaluator

Avoidance items already declare `evidencePolicy:"review"` + `verificationRequired:true` at mint. The authority machinery for review evidence shipped in fixReviewerEvidence (`review_evidence_ref` linkage, `consumer_warnings`, authority boundary at task-classifier.ts:372-395). The gap is purely that no consumer enforces the declared policy for `respects` claims. The cheapest genuinely evaluative fix is to extend `checkUnresolvedVerificationEvidence` (+ `checkCompletedTaskEvidencePlan`) to treat a task's `respects` claim on an avoidance item like an `implements`/`verifies` claim: require review-evidence authority from a non-claiming agent (adv-reviewer, task-scoped). This is evaluative (an external authority must establish compliance), not declarative — satisfying C1/DONT1.

**Authority rule for cross-policy tasks (validator C-AUTH):** a task's respects-evidence authority is determined by the REFERENCED ITEM's evidencePolicy, not the task's primary policy. A task with primary evidencePolicy "test" (e.g. an implements claim) that ALSO carries a respects ref to a review-policy avoidance item requires adv-reviewer authority FOR THAT RESPECTS CLAIM specifically — the test-policy evidence covering the implements claim does not satisfy the review-policy avoidance. The respects-evidence check is an independent per-ref requirement.

Rejected: option (a) free-form text/shape evaluator (brittle NLP over DONT text — violates P33 structural-over-heuristic). Option (c) machine-check of tool-forbidding DONT items against a tool-call log — no log exists (negative finding); deferred to its own change (OOS3).

### KD2 — D3 binds at acceptance/release gate evaluation, not at task write

Binding at write time (3 surfaces) would block legitimate task creation mid-flight and push findings to prose (violates C2). Binding at acceptance/release gate-readiness matches the existing evidence-requirement pattern (`checkUnresolvedVerificationEvidence` + `checkCompletedTaskEvidencePlan` already run there for implements/verifies; validator confirmed both are acceptance/release-only at gate-readiness.ts:710, :800). AC3's "completion/gate evaluation" both resolve at the gate in the current architecture, so binding respects evidence there is canonical. This also satisfies no-grandfathering (user decision): every task carrying a respects claim is evaluated at its next acceptance/release gate, including in-flight tasks. Transition path: missing evidence produces a typed unresolved-evidence blocker naming the DONTn/OOSn item + the remediation ("attach a task-scoped adv-reviewer report covering {id}"); never bricks persistence (D6 lesson / DONT5 — evaluation rejects the gate advance, not the report write).

Rejected: checkpoint-time binding (3 write surfaces, blocks mid-work). Write-time advisory-only (too close to declarative; agents rout past advisories).

### KD3 — D3 transition for in-flight tasks = evaluate at next gate, typed remediation, no retroactive invalidation

Completed tasks' recorded evidence is not re-litigated (OOS2). Pre-completion in-flight tasks with self-asserted respects refs become non-compliant at their next acceptance/release evaluation; the gate surfaces a typed blocker with a one-step remediation (attach reviewer evidence). Loud release-note surfacing for the activation. This honors "no grandfathering" without bricking in-flight work.

### KD4 — D6 progress substrate = per-finding fingerprint comparison, NOT narrower_retry_count

`narrower_retry_count` is a bounded (≤1) delegation-recovery counter, not a progress counter (verified). The progress-vs-retry discriminator needs a NEW per-finding novelty check in the reducer: when a BLOCKED verdict arrives, compare its blocking findings (id-first, normalized-text fingerprint fallback) against the previous round's blocking findings; if disjoint, record progress (do not increment retry_count, append to a typed `progress_rounds[]` audit field); if overlapping, increment retry_count as today. Conservative default: uncertain ⇒ count as retry. Classification is always surfaced at the doom-loop threshold regardless of progress/retry split (KD6 — no silent exemption).

**Consistency requirement (validator C-LOOPLEDGER):** `rq-loopLedger01` derives `retryFailureCount` from `error_recovery`. The retry_count semantics change must keep that projection consistent — progress rounds must NOT inflate `retryFailureCount` (a progress round is not a failure). Budgets unchanged (OOS7).

**Replay safety (validator C-REPLAY, C-SCHEMA):** `progress_rounds[]` MUST be a Zod-optional field defaulting to `[]` so histories recorded pre-change still parse and re-derive valid state (C7/DDC2). The replay-determinism suite must stay green. Validator confirmed command-level safety: no workflow handler branches on retry_count/progress_rounds to emit a command (workflows.ts:615-678 are read-projections; `readyForAcceptance` uses `incompleteTaskCount`, not retry state).

### KD5 — D6 at-budget behavior = clamp-with-warning, not silent clamp and not hard block

The shipped clamp makes over-budget writes structurally impossible, but it is silent (validator confirmed subagent-report.ts:423 emits no warning). Extend the report-side clamp site (`subagent-report.ts:419-424`) to emit an explicit `budget_warning` marker on the result when the clamp fires, and surface it in the doom-loop UX (`tool-formatters.ts:699-724`). Report submission never refuses (AC7). Raising max_retries is explicitly not the fix (DONT4).

### KD6 — D4 portfolio state = bounded store query inside create, degrade to unavailable

Add a `portfolioState` field to `ChangeCreateResult` (Zod-optional, C-SCHEMA) computed by a bounded (deadline-capped) store query inside `adv_change_create` (`change.ts:2766+`). Content: non-terminal count + never-terminal share (reuse the visibility-claim query shape triage already uses, if cheaply materialized). On read timeout/failure, emit `{ available: false }` — never block creation (AC4). Soft warning above threshold (user decision): a `nudge: "consider adv_backlog_add"` string when never-terminal share exceeds the threshold. Threshold default deferred to prep (cheap-stats check: prefer an already-materialized count over a fresh aggregate).

### KD7 — D1/D2/D5 = prose + drift-guard asset tests (test-or-cut)

Each of the five command files gains a load-bearing routing claim naming `adv_backlog_add` (+ `adv_backlog_promote` as the bridge) for out-of-scope findings, and the design risk-table reframing (D5) / MoSCoW Won't middle option (D2). Per instructions-audit test-or-cut, each claim gets a drift-guard asset test that fails if the claim text is removed or contradicted. The claim is the lever (the agent reads the contract); the test is the machine check that keeps the claim honest across refactors (AC5).

## ADR Drafts

None. No decision meets all three rubric criteria (hard-to-reverse + surprising-without-context + result-of-real-tradeoff): KD1/KD2 extend an existing pattern; KD4 is additive; KD6 is a result-shape addition. All reversible without ADR ceremony.

## Implementation Strategy

Sequence (each step independently shippable, smallest-first per the cheap-fix guidance):

1. **D2 + D5 doc edits + anchors** (smallest, no runtime risk) — adv-prep.md MoSCoW Won't path, adv-design.md risk-table reframing, each with a drift-guard asset test.
2. **D1 doc edits + anchors** — apply/review/harden (and confirm design's own routing text) gain the backlog-routing claim + asset tests.
3. **D4 portfolioState** — bounded query + degrade + nudge; unit test for the unavailable-marker path (AC4).
4. **D6 reducer progress discrimination** — per-finding fingerprint in `applySubagentReportSubmittedToState`; replay-determinism suite proof (C7); rq-loopLedger01 consistency; budget-warning marker at the clamp site (AC6, AC7).
5. **D3 respects-evidence enforcement** — extend `checkUnresolvedVerificationEvidence` (+ `checkCompletedTaskEvidencePlan`); authority-boundary reuse incl. the cross-policy rule (KD1); typed remediation blocker; acceptance/release gate tests (AC3). Largest blast radius, done last so the cheaper landings are already in.

TDD per task (P24): red test first (e.g. a task with self-asserted respects on a DONT fails acceptance; two novel-finding BLOCKEDs record progress; create with failing portfolio read returns unavailable marker).

## LBP Analysis

Long-term-best-practice alignment:
- **P33 structural-over-heuristic**: D3 enforces via the existing authority machinery, not NLP over DONT text. D6 discriminates by finding identity, not verdict counting.
- **P38 declaration-is-not-behavior**: every lever cited to its call site (paths corrected per validator); the design explicitly closes the declared-but-unenforced gap (avoidance evidencePolicy).
- **Locality (P04)**: D3 extends the function that already owns evidence requirements; D6 extends the reducer that already owns retry accounting. No new cross-cutting surface.
- **Reuse over rebuild**: fixReviewerEvidence authority boundary, the clamp, the create-result path — all extended, not replaced.
- **Campsite (P23)**: the same-class findings from the P25 scan (warrants post-mint, ContractConflictKind enum, not_applicable_reason) are surfaced but NOT silently expanded into — only the respects and retry instances are in scope.

## Affected Components

- `.opencode/command/adv-prep.md`, `adv-design.md`, `adv-apply.md`, `adv-review.md`, `adv-harden.md` + matching `*-assets.test.ts` (D1/D2/D5)
- `plugin/src/temporal/gate-readiness.ts` (`checkUnresolvedVerificationEvidence` + `checkCompletedTaskEvidencePlan` extension — D3)
- `plugin/src/validator/task-classifier.ts` (authority boundary reuse — D3; no schema break)
- `plugin/src/types/evidence-policy.ts` (authority resolution reuse — D3)
- `plugin/src/tools/task.ts` (no change to write surfaces; respects already stored)
- `plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts` (`applySubagentReportSubmittedToState` — D6 progress discrimination)
- `plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts` (`:419-424` clamp site — D6 budget warning)
- `plugin/src/utils/tool-formatters.ts` (`:699-724` doom-loop UX — D6 surface classification)
- `plugin/src/types/tasks.ts` (additive `progress_rounds[]` audit field, Zod-optional default `[]` + fingerprint helpers — D6)
- `plugin/src/tools/change.ts` (`:2766+` create result) + `plugin/src/storage/store-types.ts` (`ChangeCreateResult.portfolioState`, Zod-optional — D4)
- Spec deltas: `rq-findingRouting01`, `rq-respectsEvaluation01`, `rq-createPortfolioLine01`, `rq-retryProgressAccounting01` (advance-workflow spec); confirm consistency with `rq-loopLedger01`

## Design-Derived Criteria

Technical criteria caused by the chosen architecture (no new user-facing AC):

- **DDC1**: D3 enforcement read at gate-readiness must complete within the existing gate-eval time budget; a respects-evidence check must not add an unbounded scan (bound to the task's contract_refs.respects list, which is small).
- **DDC2**: D6 fingerprint comparison must be deterministic (replay-safe) — normalized-text fingerprint is a pure function of finding text; no Date/Math.random in the path (Temporal determinism). `progress_rounds[]` is Zod-optional default `[]`.
- **DDC3**: D4 portfolioState query is deadline-capped (e.g. ≤ existing 8s store read budget); on any miss the field is `{available:false}` and creation proceeds.
- **DDC4**: D6 reducer change preserves the clamp's invariant (retry_count ≤ max_retries) and the monotonic true attempt number inside each `attempts[].attempt_number`; rq-loopLedger01 `retryFailureCount` stays consistent (progress rounds do not inflate it).
- **DDC5**: Asset-test anchors (D1/D2/D5) cite the exact claim string; refactors that rephrase must update both the claim and the test in one commit (test-or-cut). Paths in citations corrected per validator C-PATHS.

## Risks / Mitigations

- **R1 — D3 no-grandfathering stalls in-flight work**: in-flight tasks with self-asserted refs block at next acceptance/release. Mitigation: typed one-step remediation blocker (KD3), loud release-note surfacing, completed tasks excluded (OOS2). Residual: some in-flight changes need a reviewer pass; this is the intended cost of no-grandfathering (user decision).
- **R2 — D6 fingerprint instability misclassifies a repeated failure as progress**: reviewer re-words the same finding. Mitigation: id-first + normalized-text fallback + uncertain⇒retry (KD4); classification surfaced at doom-loop threshold either way (KD6). Residual: rare false-progress; visible, not silent.
- **R3 — D6 progress exemption becomes the escape hatch**: an agent rationalizing produces "new" findings each round. Mitigation: cap not on progress rounds but on mandatory user surface at threshold regardless of split (KD6); the guard's escalation path is unchanged.
- **R4 — D4 portfolio read adds create-time latency under contention**: store reads already time out under multi-session load (observed). Mitigation: deadline-capped query + unavailable marker (KD6, DDC3); the line degrades honestly.
- **R5 — D3 extension introduces a false positive**: a legitimate task textually resembles a DONT. Mitigation: enforcement requires review EVIDENCE (authority judgement), not a text match — the reviewer resolves ambiguity, mirroring how implements/verifies evidence works today.
- **R6 — D3 cross-policy authority ambiguity (validator C-AUTH)**: a test-policy task carrying a respects ref to a review-policy avoidance could pass on its test evidence alone. Mitigation: per-ref authority rule (KD1) — the respects claim requires adv-reviewer authority independent of the task's primary policy.

## Prep-confirm items (small, non-blocking)

- Exact file:line of one per-command asset test asserting command-file content (anchor shape for AC5) — confirm at prep.
- AC7 verify (validator C-AC7VERIFY): confirm no current submit path hard-blocks at retry budget post-clamp (design's own prep-confirm) — quick read of the submit-path result construction.
- D4 threshold default + whether a never-terminal share is cheaply materialized (visibility-claim query reuse) — prep cheap-stats check.

## Validator Result

**Status: `caution`** (medium confidence, medium risk; no fail-level blockers). Validator: adv-researcher, reportId `fixFindingRouting|change:researcher:design-validation|adv-researcher|1`.

Validator confirmed: KD1 authority boundary holds (claiming agents cannot self-assert); KD2 gate-binding matches the existing pattern (both evidence checks are acceptance/release-only); KD4 substrate correctly identified; KD5/KD6 additive claims verified; replay safe at command level; spec-law consistent (rq-contractTrace01, rq-PR010/rq-PR008, rq-ADVEXEC06, rq-backlogDurability01).

6 in-scope cautions, all folded into the design above:
- **C-AUTH** → KD1 cross-policy authority rule added + R6.
- **C-LOOPLEDGER** → KD4 consistency requirement + DDC4.
- **C-REPLAY** → KD4 replay-safety note + DDC2.

- **C-AC7VERIFY** → retained as a prep-confirm item.

# Executive Summary: Fix Finding Routing

## Outcome

Mid-lifecycle findings now have a friction-free durable home in the backlog, avoidance/out-of-scope respects claims require independent review verification before acceptance, retry accounting distinguishes productive review rounds from failed retries, and the retry budget clamp is visible rather than silent.

## Why It Matters

ADV had a claims-vs-facts gap: command contracts told agents to route findings to the backlog, but nothing structural enforced it; avoidance items declared review-evidence requirements that nothing checked; every BLOCKED verdict counted as a retry regardless of whether it surfaced new ground; and the retention clamp that bounded retry history dropped entries silently. Together these meant the system could assert compliance it hadn't verified and miscount progress as failure.

## What Was Verified

- 31 new tests across 5 test files (change-state, gate-readiness, tool-formatters, portfolio-state, finding-routing-assets) — all green
- Red/green TDD cycles recorded for every code task
- Full suite: 305/305 targeted + 20/20 replay determinism + `pnpm run check` clean
- Typecheck clean across all changes
- Schema regeneration verified (change.schema.json, task.schema.json)
- Drift-guard asset tests confirm routing claims fail on removal
- Acceptance review: adv-reviewer multi-dimensional review, verdict APPROVED (formatting fixes applied)

## What Was Delivered

- **Finding routing** (T1/T2): prep, design, apply, review, and harden command contracts now name `adv_backlog_add` as the durable middle-tier option, each with a drift-guard asset test
- **Portfolio state** (T3): `adv_change_create` surfaces bounded portfolio stats (open count, never-terminal share, soft nudge above threshold) with graceful degradation to `{available: false}`
- **Progress-vs-retry** (T4): BLOCKED verdicts with disjoint findings are recorded as progress, not retries — error_recovery is not inflated
- **Budget warning** (T5): the retention clamp emits a visible `budget_warning` marker; submission never refuses at/over budget; doom-loop UX surfaces it
- **Respects authority** (T6): gate-readiness blocks acceptance/release for tasks respecting DONT/OOS items without task-scoped adv-reviewer authority; no grandfathering
- **Spec deltas** (T7): four requirements staged (rq-findingRouting01, rq-respectsEvaluation01, rq-createPortfolioLine01, rq-retryProgressAccounting01) + CHANGELOG

## Risks / Follow-ups

- The respects-authority check (T6) will block ANY change's acceptance if done tasks respect DONT/OOS items without per-task reviewer reports. This is the intended enforcement, but teams should be aware that `/adv-review` must produce per-task reports.
- The portfolio read at create time adds a bounded (2s deadline) Temporal query to every `adv_change_create` call. Degradation is explicit, but the latency is additive.

## Release Readiness Summary

- **Ops readiness**: READY. No deployment, migration, or infrastructure changes. Plugin codebase change only — deploy via standard `scripts/deploy-local.sh` from merged trunk after archive.
- **Migration/data impact**: N/A. No schema migrations, data format changes, or stored-state breaking changes. All new Zod fields are optional (budget_warning, progress_rounds, portfolioState, ChangePortfolioState).
- **Frontend/preview impact**: N/A. No frontend/UI changes.
- **Collision/release risk**: LOW. Merge compatibility verified (clean dry-run merge into trunk). No concurrent changes touching the same files. Reviewer APPROVED with 1 formatting fix (applied).
- **Open follow-ups**: None blocking. The respects-authority enforcement (T6) is a behavioral change that affects all future changes' acceptance gates — documented in spec delta rq-respectsEvaluation01.
- **Next action**: `/adv-archive fixFindingRouting`
